 At Indore

sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Nitin Nanoreya - advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Vinod Thakur appearing on behalf of Advocate Gen  Shri Raghunandan Soni, learned counsel for the respon  ORDER Heard and perused the record.
2. This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail.

The applicant is arrested in relation to Crime/FIR No.110/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Simrol District- Indore for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 34 of IPC and 5l/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in custody since 10.03.2024.
3. As per allegation, the applicant has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
The age of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26735 2 MCRC-39279-2024 prosecutrix was more than 17 years and 2 months at the time of incident.
As per the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, she has not stated anything regarding commission of rape.
He also submits that the prosecutrix has no objection for grant of bail to the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 10.03.2024 nearly one month.
Final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the complainant has expressed his no objection for grant of bail to the applicant.
6. Learned Govt. Advocate for the State opposed the prayer and prays for its rejection.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and custody period of the applicant, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:26735 3 MCRC-39279-2024 480(3) of BNSS.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Vijay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116499764/
